title: Sunny and the Bush Mouse
description: Little Sonny the quokka meets a quick, bright-eyed bush mouse going about its busy day. A gentle, sweet bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny was sitting very quietly near the old log pile at the edge of the clearing when he noticed something small moving in the leaf litter.

A tiny bush mouse.

It was barely bigger than Sunny's paw. Its ears were round and enormous for such a small face. Its eyes were like two small shining beads of jet.

It moved in quick little bursts — dart, stop, sniff, dart, stop — weaving between the fallen leaves and twigs with tremendous purpose.

Sunny watched, completely still.

The mouse found a seed, sat up on its hind legs, and held it in its tiny front paws to eat. Its nose twitched constantly. Its long tail curled behind it in the dust.

Sunny thought it was absolutely wonderful.

Such a small creature, doing such important work. Finding its food. Going about its day. Not worried about anything else, just this seed, just right now.

The mouse finished eating, cleaned its whiskers with its paws — very thoroughly, in tiny quick circles — and then darted off again into the undergrowth.

Sunny sat for a while longer, looking at the small patch of ground where the mouse had been.

He felt peaceful. He felt grateful, somehow, for being a witness to such a small and ordinary and wonderful thing.

He breathed in the smell of the leaf litter and the dry earth.

He let his eyes grow heavy.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, tiny bush mouse. Goodnight, small and wonderful world.
